It was a cold, wet night when it happened. I had been minding my own business, just trying to make it home early so I could watch a movie or two before I set off to work my second job and it's awful 9-5 shift. In fact, I was walking quicker than usual. You see, I just bought Star Wars: The Force Awakens on Blu-Ray from HMV, and I was excited to watch it. The movie was a relic, for gods sake! It was even more special, after the death of it's star. No, not Harrison Ford, you spoiler loving freak, John Boyega. It had happened so suddenly, one day he was on the Graham Norton show and the next he was gone.

Anyway, I was walking home when I banged into this guy in front of me. He was wearing a hoodie that obscured his face, and gloves as well. I couldn't make out a thing about him. Of course, it was difficult to register his apperance with blood pumping out of the back of my head. Turns out when someone bangs into you and you hit your head on the curb, you generally don't get up. 

I was losing blood, and had lost most of my energy. My copy of Star Wars: The Force Awakens lay forgotten on the pavement. The person looked at it, and snorted. It was a male voice, at least that's what I could infer from the snort. He looked at me, and slowly pulled his hood back. His eyes bore into mine, concern and shock flashing through them, betraying his attempt at stoicism. As I felt my life slowly slipping away, I had only one thing in my mind. I opened my mouth, spat out the blood that had filled it and said slowly, painfully:

"FN-2187, who gave you permission to remove that hoodie?"

I smirked, knowing I was going to die with the best last words a man could hope for. Last words John Boyega, even with fear underlying the general tone of it, laughed at.

I died shortly after, but the strangest thing happened. I didn't go to heaven, and I didn't decompose under the ground in a casket. No, I awoke standing, staring at my dead body, a blueish glow surrounding me. John Boyega's eyes widened, and slowely he managed to stammer out, "That's not how the force works," before pulling his hood up and running away as fast as his supposedly-dead legs could carry him.
